body:
A dearth of private equity exits and increased withdrawals has driven Partners Group to split its $10.67 billion evergreen fund.

Swiss-headquartered Partners Group is considered one of the pioneers of evergreen funds — open-ended vehicles that give investors exposure to private markets without locking away their money for an extended period. It launched one of the first in 2001.

Now, 25 years later, it is proposing to split its EUR6.6 billion ($10.67 billion) Global Value Fund into two in a first-of-its-kind move. The proposal aims to address the rise in popularity of evergreen funds, a lack of private equity exits and the need for liquidity.

“If you go back seven years ago, there weren’t any [other] evergreen funds. We were it. But in the last three or four years there’s been more of a challenging fundraising environment which has led to more evergreen funds,” Partners Group head of Australia Martin Scott told Capital Brief.

“We’ve seen a lot of people re-weighting portfolios because of that.”

In June, the fund capped investor redemptions at 5% per quarter, citing difficult private market conditions driven by macroeconomic shifts and geopolitical challenges.

Now, it is proposing to split the fund into two components: a compounding sleeve comprising newer-vintage businesses, which account for around 23% of the fund, and a distributing sleeve comprising older vintages.

The newer vintage sleeve will continue to invest while older vintages will distribute capital as private equity exits come through.
